title: What is not of grace is of works—so sanctification is not of works
source_text: XXXVI. Primo enim, secundum Pauli doctrinam, & loquendi modum, id quod gratiae non est, ex operibus est. Quippe res sunt oppositae, & quae se invicem destruunt, gratiam esse, & esse ex operibus. Si autem gratia, inquit Apostolus, jam non ex operibus. Alioquin gratia, jam non est gratia. Si ex operibus, jam non est gratia: quandoquidem opus, jam non est opus. Rom. 11. 6. Hominis autem sanctificationem, esse donum Dei gratuitum, & gratiam plane singularem, nemo est qui possit in dubium vocare, ac proinde, juxta Apostoli doctrinam, ex operibus non est.
pass_a_gloss: For first, according to Paul's doctrine and manner of speaking, that which is not of grace is of works. For the things are opposed and destroy each other: to be of grace, and to be of works. But if of grace, says the Apostle, then no longer of works. Otherwise grace is no longer grace. If of works, then it is no longer grace: since the work is no longer a work. Rom. 11:6. But that man's sanctification is a free gift of God and a plainly singular grace, there is no one who can call into doubt, and therefore, according to the Apostle's doctrine, it is not of works.
pass_b_english: Paul: grace and works mutually exclude (Rom 11:6).
Sanctification is free singular grace—hence not of works.

choices.why: Opposite of grace in Pauline antithesis.
